safety.config.fix: How to fix: change the value in that file to meet the condition above, then run `wb-config validate` again.
explain.rule.override: higher layer wins (personal > plugin option > machine > project > default)
explain.rule.union: union of every layer (cannot be removed)
init.q.gate: Full verification command (leave empty if none)
init.gitignore: Note: `{pattern}` in .gitignore blocks `{path}`. Add the exception line `!{path}`.
init.notGit: Not a git repository. Skipping the state folder and exclude entry.
init.uiHint: This project has a UI. You can install UI stability checks with `/wb:ui-check`.
init.done: Initialization finished. Run `/wb:doctor` to review the result.
doctor.title: wb check
doctor.codegraph.missing: not installed. `/wb:init` installs it only after you agree
safety.where: Run `/wb:doctor` or read the "Safety hooks" section of the README. Only the repository owner can change these rules.
safety.git.unresolved.why: The target folder or command of `{cmd}` cannot be known before it runs (variable or command substitution).
safety.git.unresolved.fix: Write the path and the git subcommand literally and run it again, e.g. `git -C /absolute/path commit -m "..."`.
safety.git.lane_commit.why: A lane may only commit on its own lane branch ({own}). The current branch is `{branch}`.
safety.git.lane_commit.fix: Commit from your own lane worktree. The main checkout, the integration branch and other lanes' branches belong to the main session.
safety.git.lane_merge.why: A lane may only merge or rebase the latest integration branch into its own branch ({own}); current branch `{branch}`.
safety.git.lane_merge.fix: Name the integration branch explicitly, e.g. `git rebase <integration branch>`. Leave other merges to the main session.
safety.git.lane_push.fix: Commit on your own branch and report. The main session integrates and pushes.
safety.git.lane_switch.why: A lane may not switch to another branch (current `{branch}`).
safety.git.lane_switch.fix: Stay on your lane branch. To restore files only, use `git checkout -- <file>` or `git restore <file>`.
safety.git.stash.why: The stash list is shared with other sessions and worktrees; an unnamed stash or pop can take or drop someone else's changes.
safety.git.stash.fix: Use a temporary WIP commit, or `git stash push -u -m "<unique name>"` and restore with `git stash apply <sha>`.
safety.git.reset_hard.why: `git reset --hard` discards uncommitted changes for good (current `{branch}`).
safety.git.reset_hard.fix: Check what would be lost with `git status` first and leave a WIP commit if needed.
safety.git.clean.why: `git clean -f` deletes untracked files for good.
safety.git.branch_protected.why: The protected branch `{target}` cannot be deleted, moved or force-recreated.
safety.git.branch_protected.fix: Leave protected branches alone. If it must change, the repository owner runs it directly.
safety.git.branch_delete.why: This deletes or overwrites branch `{target}`. Unmerged commits can be lost.
safety.git.branch_delete.fix: Check for unmerged commits with `git log {target} --not --remotes`.
safety.git.ref.why: Editing branch refs directly bypasses the merge rules.
safety.git.ref.fix: Use the regular commands such as `git merge` or `git branch`.
safety.git.gate_locked.why: A verification gate is running (gate lock present). Merges wait until it finishes.
safety.git.gate_locked.fix: Run it again after the gate finishes. If the gate crashed, check the lock with `/wb:doctor`.
safety.git.main_merge.why: The protected branch `{branch}` takes a single source, and only with an owner grant.
safety.git.main_merge.fix: Name one branch to merge, have the repository owner type `/wb:approve merge-main <branch>`, then run it again.
safety.git.force_push.why: Force pushes (--force, --force-with-lease, +refspec) are not allowed for anyone.
safety.git.force_push.fix: Integrate the remote first (e.g. `git pull --rebase`) and push normally.
safety.git.push_all.fix: Name each branch to push, e.g. `git push origin <branch>`.
safety.git.push_feature.why: Feature branch pushes need confirmation (setting `project.git.feature_push: ask`).
safety.git.push_feature.fix: Confirm the push. To always allow it, set `git.feature_push` to `allow` in `.wb/config.json`.
safety.git.push_feature_denied.why: This project blocks pushes from agents (`project.git.feature_push: deny`).
safety.grant.missing.why: This action ({action}) on the protected branch `{branch}` needs an owner grant, and there is none.
safety.grant.missing.fix: The repository owner must type `/wb:approve {action}` in the prompt (15 minutes, one use, one commit). Agents cannot create grants.
safety.grant.action.why: The current grant is for a different action (needed: {action}).
safety.grant.used.why: The grant has already been used. Grants are single-use.
safety.grant.used.fix: If it is needed again, the repository owner types `/wb:approve {action}` again.
safety.grant.expired.fix: The repository owner must type `/wb:approve {action}` again.
safety.grant.head.why: The granted commit ({granted}) differs from the commit being applied ({head}).
safety.grant.head.fix: The branch moved after the grant. Review it again; the repository owner types `/wb:approve {action}` again.
safety.stamp.missing.why: There is no gate pass stamp for commit {head}.
safety.stamp.missing.fix: Run the project gate (`project.gate.command`) to a full pass on this commit, then run it again.
safety.stamp.head.why: The gate pass stamp belongs to another commit (needed: {head}).
safety.stamp.head.fix: Pass the gate again on this commit.
safety.gh.lane_merge.why: Lanes may not merge pull requests.
safety.gh.lane_merge.fix: Put the PR number in your report and leave the merge to the main session.
safety.gh.unresolved.why: The PR's base branch could not be determined, so the merge is blocked.
safety.gh.unresolved.fix: Check that `gh pr view <number>` works. A PR into a protected branch also needs `/wb:approve merge-main` first.
safety.kill.pattern.why: Killing by name or pattern (`{cmd}`) can take down other sessions' or the owner's servers.
safety.kill.pattern.fix: Find the PID of the process you started and use `kill <PID>`.
safety.kill.protected_port.fix: Protected-port servers belong to the owner. Use your lane ports (`wb-port get`).
safety.kill.unresolved.why: The target PID of `{cmd}` cannot be checked in advance, so protected ports cannot be ruled out.
safety.kill.unresolved.fix: Write the PID as a number and run it again.
safety.rm.dynamic.why: The `rm -r` target `{target}` depends on a variable or an unknown folder, so what it deletes is unknown.
safety.rm.dynamic.fix: Write the path to delete as an absolute path.
safety.rm.broad.why: Removing `{target}` wipes the home folder, a system folder or the whole project.
safety.rm.broad.fix: Name the exact subfolder to remove.
safety.rm.git.why: `{target}` is inside a git repository's internal folder.
safety.rm.git.fix: Clean up with git commands such as `git worktree remove` or `git gc`.
safety.rm.outside.fix: Make sure the path is safe to remove. Keep temporary files in a temp folder or inside the project.
safety.browser.headed.why: A browser that opens a window (`{cmd}`) steals focus from the person using the machine.
safety.browser.headed.fix: Add `--headless=new`, or run Playwright in its default headless mode. If a window is really needed, the owner runs it directly.
safety.browser.open.fix: Capture with a headless browser and share the result file.
safety.browser.playwright_window.fix: Use a headless run (`npx playwright test`) and the result files (trace, report).
safety.paths.state.why: `{path}` is a wb state file (owner grant, gate stamp, lane ledger). Only hooks and wb tools write it.
safety.paths.state.fix: Grants come from `/wb:approve` and stamps from a gate run. Do not edit them by hand.
safety.paths.protected.fix: Ask the repository owner if it must change. See the list with `wb-config explain project.protected_paths`.
safety.paths.config.why: `{path}` is a wb settings file. Changing it can change the safety rules.
safety.paths.config.fix: Review the change before going ahead, then check it with `wb-config validate`.
safety.shell.unresolved.why: The command name is a variable or substitution (`{cmd}`), so it cannot be judged before it runs.
safety.shell.unresolved.fix: Write the command name literally, e.g. `git push ...`.
safety.config.broken.why: wb settings have an error, so safety checks cannot run: {file} · {key}: {msg}
safety.config.broken.fix: Fix the settings file and check it with `wb-config validate`. Until then git changes, kills, deletes and browser runs are blocked.
safety.approve.model.why: `/wb:approve` works only when a person types it in the prompt.
safety.approve.model.fix: Ask the repository owner to type `/wb:approve <action>`.
safety.internal.why: The safety hook failed internally and blocked this call: {msg}
safety.internal.fix: Check the installation with `/wb:doctor`. If it keeps happening, report it with the error text.
approve.config_broken: No grant was created because the settings have an error: {file} · {key}. Check with `wb-config validate`.
approve.not_git: Grants can only be created inside a git repository.
approve.need_ref: Cannot tell which branch {action} is for. Name it: `/wb:approve {action} <branch>`.
approve.bad_ref: `{ref}` does not resolve to a commit.
approve.stamp_needed: A gate pass stamp for the same commit is also required: {stamp}
approve.granted: Owner grant recorded: {action} · {ref} · commit {head} · {ttl} min (expires {expires}) · one use. Only this commit can be applied.
chat.detailed: [wb] Reply guideline: in chat, give the contents, evidence and figures directly and in detail. Attach evidence as an artifact or file as well.
chat.summary: [wb] Reply guideline: keep chat replies short (result and decision first). Put evidence and detail in an artifact or file and link it.
handoff.start:
[wb handoff] Session start ({src}). This project has a handoff file ({file}).
Do the following. 1) Read the excerpt below (newest section); read the whole file when needed. 2) In your first reply, summarize the current state: done / in progress / next / open questions / pitfalls. 3) Then start the work.

--- {file} excerpt (newest section) ---
{excerpt}
--- end of excerpt (full file: {path}) ---
handoff.stop: [wb handoff] Work newer than {file} was detected (a commit or a changed file). Update the handoff in {file} and then finish: done / in progress / next / open questions / pitfalls (keep still-valid items, newest section on top). After updating, tell the user that the session can be cleared (/clear). If this turn's change needs no handoff, state the reason in one line and finish.
token.shrink: [wb token guard] Usage in the last {hours} hours reached {util}% of the budget. From now on split waves and turns into shorter units; keep a committable stable state at the end of each unit.
token.handoff: [wb token guard] Usage in the last {hours} hours reached {util}% of the budget. Keep waves and turns short and update the handoff file at the end of every wave.
token.handoff.guarded: [wb token guard] Usage in the last {hours} hours reached {util}% of the budget. Keep waves and turns short. The handoff guard asks for a handoff at the end of every wave; follow it immediately.
token.critical: [wb token guard] Usage in the last {hours} hours is {util}% of the budget: critical. Stop at a safe point now and finish the last handoff. Then notify the user and start no new work; ask whether to (a) wait for the automatic resume or (b) switch session, and wait. This percentage is a local estimate; check the exact value with /usage.
token.notify.title: wb token guard
token.notify.body: {util}% of the budget used in the last {hours} hours. Hand off, then wait.
token.toggled.off: Token guard is off: stage detection and instructions are stopped.
token.calibrate.usage: Usage: wb-token calibrate [<weighted tokens>] (default: current usage of the window). Run it when the app shows the limit reached.
token.status.usage: Last {hours} hours (local transcripts, this machine only): output {output}, input {input}, cache read {cache_read}, cache write {cache_creation} ({msgs} replies). Weighted total {weighted} (= input + 1.25 cache write + 0.1 cache read + 5 output).
token.status.uncalibrated: Budget not set (personal.token_guard.budget = 0): the guard is silent. Run `wb-token calibrate` when the app shows the limit reached. Exact usage: /usage.
retry.prompt: The previous work was interrupted by a usage limit. Continue the interrupted work to the end. If it is already complete, change nothing and only report the completed state.
retry.notify.title: wb automatic resume
retry.notify.scheduled: Usage limit reached. Automatic resume scheduled for {at}.
retry.notify.off: Automatic resume is off, so the resume was skipped (wb-retry on to enable).
retry.notify.downgraded: bypassPermissions is not confirmed; resuming with the default permission mode (wb-retry mode).
retry.notify.start: Limit reset: resuming the interrupted work.
retry.notify.failed: Resume failed (exit {code}). See the log in the wb data folder (auto-retry/logs).
retry.notify.done: Work resumed. Continue in chat with: claude --resume {session}
retry.session.off: [wb auto-retry] off: no automatic resume after a usage limit. Turn on with `wb-retry on`.
retry.session.done: [wb auto-retry] {count} finished automatic resume(s). Details: `wb-retry status`.
retry.status.off: Automatic resume: off (detection and resume are stopped)
retry.status.downgraded: (bypassPermissions is set but not confirmed, so default is used)
retry.toggled.off: Automatic resume is off: detection stops, and scheduled resumes are skipped.
retry.cancel.usage: Usage: wb-retry status | on | off | cancel <session id prefix|all> | mode <mode> | limits
retry.mode.warning: bypassPermissions lets the resumed session run any tool without asking, unattended. Use it only in folders you trust. To accept this risk, run: wb-retry mode bypassPermissions --i-understand
retry.mode.set: Permission mode of the resumed session: {mode}
terse.on: Terse mode is on for this repository.
terse.off: Terse mode is off for this repository.
terse.notGit: Not a git repository: the switch needs one. Set personal.terse in ~/.wb/personal.json instead.
dispatch.where: `wb-route explain <task>` shows the routing trace and `wb-check brief <file>` checks a brief. Run `/wb:doctor` to inspect settings.
dispatch.notify.title: wb dispatch on hold
dispatch.config_error.why: A settings file has an error ({file} {key}: {msg}). Routing was judged with the defaults.
dispatch.config_error.fix: Run `/wb:doctor` to find and fix the error.
dispatch.brief_missing.why: No brief marker (`<!-- wb-brief v1 type=… lane=… -->`). A dispatch needs a brief.
dispatch.brief_missing.fix: Write a brief from `templates/briefs/` (impl, fix, mockup, research, review, docs, test) and paste it into the prompt or name the brief file.
dispatch.brief_incomplete.fix: Fill in the missing sections or statements and dispatch again. `wb-check brief <file>` checks it beforehand.
dispatch.brief_placeholder.why: The brief still has an unfilled placeholder `{{{name}}}`.
dispatch.brief_placeholder.fix: Replace every `{{…}}` placeholder of the template with a real value.
dispatch.type_unknown.why: The brief task type `{type}` is not in the routing table.
dispatch.type_unknown.fix: Set type= in the marker to one of: {known}.
dispatch.type_missing.why: The task type is unknown and no model was given.
dispatch.type_missing.fix: Add type= to the brief marker ({known}). `wb-route resolve <task>` tells you which model to use.
dispatch.model_missing.why: No model given. Routing for task `{task}` picks `{model}`.
dispatch.model_missing.fix: Pass model: "{model}" to the Agent call.
dispatch.model_unknown.why: Model `{model}` is not in the routing table.
dispatch.model_denied.why: Model `{model}` is on the denied list (routing.denied). Denied beats routing.
dispatch.model_denied.fix: Use the next model in the chain, `{next}`. To lift the ban, remove it from denied in `~/.wb/routing.json`.
dispatch.model_exhausted.fix: Use the next model in the chain, `{next}`.
dispatch.below_floor.why: Model `{model}` is below the floor `{floor}` of task `{task}`.
dispatch.below_floor.fix: Use `{next}`. Routing never goes below the floor.
dispatch.differ_violation.why: This task must use a model different from the implementer, and `{model}` is the implementer's model.
dispatch.off_chain.why: Model `{model}` is not in the chain of task `{task}` ({chain}).
dispatch.off_chain.fix: Use `{next}`, or fix type= in the brief marker if the task type is wrong.
dispatch.not_first.why: Model `{model}` is allowed, but routing's first choice is `{next}`.
dispatch.not_first.fix: Use `{next}` unless there is a specific reason.
dispatch.same_model.why: No model other than the implementer's is left, so `{model}` runs in a fresh context.
dispatch.same_model.fix: Have the lane report state that the review used the same model in a fresh context.
dispatch.wait.why: Task `{task}` never goes below `{floor}`. Waiting until the reset at {until}.
dispatch.wait.fix: Dispatch again after the reset. Use `/model` to switch the main session model.
dispatch.no_model.why: No usable model is left in the chain of task `{task}` ({chain}) after the denied list and the floor.
dispatch.no_model.fix: Check denied and the chain in `~/.wb/routing.json`. Use `/model` to switch the main session model.
dispatch.lanes_full.why: {count} lanes are live, the cap is {max}; the new lane `{lane}` cannot start.
dispatch.lanes_full.fix: Integrate and clean up finished lanes first. The cap is machine.lanes.max.
route.head: Task {task} · chain {chain} · floor {floor}
route.note.same-model-fresh-context: no other model left; {model} in a fresh context (record it in the report)
route.result_wait: Result: do not dispatch — never below {floor}, waiting until {until}
route.result_none: Result: no usable model (check denied and the floor)
route.unknown_task: Task {task} is not in the routing table.
safety.slot.unwrapped.why: `{cmd}` competes with other lanes for the machine when run outside a slot ({kinds}).
slot.guard.warn: `{cmd}` is a heavy run and should go through a slot ({kinds}). Run it again wrapped like this: `{wrap}`
slot.config_error: Stopped on a settings error: {key} in {file} — {msg}. Check it with `wb-config validate`.
slot.usage: Usage: wb-slot [--kind heavy|browser|heavy,browser] [--lane <id>] [--timeout <sec>] -- <command> | wb-slot status | wb-slot reap
slot.wait_load: Waiting: load is high (1-minute load {load}, threshold {max}).
slot.wait_busy: Waiting: all {count} {kind} slots are in use.
slot.timeout: No slot within {sec} seconds; the command was not run.
port.usage: Usage: wb-port get <name> [--lane <id>] | list | lease --lane <id> | release --lane <id> | check
port.no-lane: The lane is unknown. Add `--lane <id>` or run inside a lane worktree.
port.no-lease: Lane {lane} has no port lease. Lease one first with `wb-port lease --lane {lane}`.
port.unknown-name: No port named {name}. Use a protected port name or lane.<name> (machine.ports.lane_range.per_lane).
port.list_range: Lane range: base {base}, step {step}, names {names}, up to {max} lanes
port.problem.overlap: The lane step ({step}) is smaller than the ports per lane ({names}), so bands overlap.
port.problem.too-high: The last lane port ({last}) is above 65535.
port.problem.protected: Band {block} holds protected port {name} ({port}); that band is never assigned.
port.full: No free lane port band (max {max}). Clear finished leases with `wb-reap --apply` or widen machine.ports.lane_range.
wt.git_failed.fix: Check the message above, sort out the branch or path, then run again.
wt.integration_ambiguous.why: Several branches match the integration branch pattern: {branches}
wt.bad_id.why: `{id}` cannot be used as a lane name.
wt.bad_id.fix: Use up to 64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-` (for example l3).
wt.lanes_full.why: {count} live lanes reach the limit of {max} ({lanes}).
wt.lanes_full.fix: Remove finished lanes with `wb-worktree remove <id>` first. The limit is machine.lanes.max.
wt.path_exists.fix: Pass another `--path` or clear that folder.
wt.main_checkout.why: {path} is the main checkout and is never removed.
wt.main_checkout.fix: Name a lane worktree or its path.
wt.busy.why: Processes are running inside {path}, so it was not removed (PID {pids}).
wt.busy.fix: Check each PID above and stop it with `kill <PID>` (not pkill or killall, which match by name). Then run again.
wt.dirty.fix: Commit what you want to keep. Add `--force` only to throw the rest away.
wt.not_worktree.why: {path} is not a worktree of this repository, so it was not removed.
wt.not_worktree.fix: Check the path with `git worktree list`. wb never deletes a folder that is not a worktree.
wt.config.fix: Check and fix it with `wb-config validate`.
wt.created: Created the worktree of lane {id}: {path} (branch {branch}, base {base} {sha})
wt.setup_failed: Setup command failed (exit {status}): {cmd}. The worktree was kept.
wt.setup_skipped: No slot came free, so the setup command was skipped. Run `wb-worktree setup {id}` later.
wt.removed: Removed the worktree {path} (ports released {ports}, unregistered {lanes}, branch deleted {branch})
reap.lease_dropped: Dropped the port lease of {lane} ({path} is gone)
reap.lane_dropped: Removed {lane} from the lane registry ({path} is gone)
reap.gate_stale: gate.lock has been there for {ageMin} min. If no gate is running, remove it with `wb-reap --gate-lock`.
wthook.synced_on: Registered the Claude Code worktree hooks in {file} (project.worktree.hook: true). They apply from the next session.
wthook.synced_off: Removed the Claude Code worktree hooks from {file} (project.worktree.hook: false). Claude Code's own behaviour returns from the next session.
wthook.conflict: {file} already has another WorktreeCreate hook, so the wb hooks were not registered. Only one can run; decide which to keep and remove the other.
init.worktreeHook: Registered hooks in {file} so wb also creates Claude Code's worktrees (claude --worktree, subagent isolation).
init.worktreeHookKept: Kept the existing .wb/config.json. To turn the worktree hooks on, add "worktree": {"hook": true} to it and run `wb-worktree hooks sync`.
config.fix: How to fix: change that key in the file above to meet the condition, then check again with `wb-config validate`.

ledger.err.waves.bad_result: Unknown result "{result}". Use pass, fail or skip.
ledger.err.numbers.no_series: No number series "{series}" in .wb/config.json (known: {known}). Declare it under "numbers" with dir, pattern, width.
ledger.err.numbers.not_reserved: Number {n} of series {series} is not reserved.
ledger.err.cases.bad_module: Invalid module name "{module}" (lowercase letters, digits, hyphen).
ledger.err.cases.no_module: No case file for module "{module}" ({file}). Create it with `wb-cases init`.
ledger.err.cases.bad_priority: Unknown priority "{priority}". Use P0 to P3.
ledger.err.cases.bad_status: Unknown case status "{status}". Use active or fixme.
ledger.err.defects.bad_severity: Unknown severity "{severity}". Use critical, high, medium or low.
ledger.err.defects.bad_status: Unknown defect status "{status}". Use fixed or wontfix.
waves.returned: Lane {lane} sent back ({count} time(s) so far). Dispatch it again with a fix brief.
board.empty: No waves recorded yet. Create one with `wb-waves init-wave`.
resume.stale.progress_stale: {file} is older than the latest work. Update it before new work.
resume.stale.lane_dead: Lane {lane} is marked running but has had no activity for {min} min.
resume.stale.lane_dirty: Lane {lane}: {count} uncommitted change(s) in its worktree.
resume.stale.worktree_unregistered: Worktree {path} ({branch}) is not in the lane registry.
resume.stale.dispatch_orphan: A {type} dispatch for lane {lane} never started an agent.

resume.prompt.nobrief: No brief file recorded; ask the controller for it.
resume.prompt.worktree: Worktree: {path} (last commit: {last}). Keep the existing changes there.

cases.retired: Retired case {id}. The id is not reused.
cases.ok: Case ledger and defect register are consistent.

cases.problem.bad_status: {module} {id}: status "{status}" is not active or fixme.

tr.none: No test result workbook found ({dir}). Create one with `wb-test-report run`.

tr.check.how: Fix: run `wb-test-report run` to create the workbook and the summary json, then commit both. For ledger mismatches, read the ledger comparison sheet and fix the ledger or the test.

tr.check.no_git: Not a git repository, so the commit state was not checked.
tr.check.head_ok: The run commit {run} matches the current HEAD.
tr.check.head_differs: The run commit {run} differs from the current HEAD {head}. Run the verification again for an integration or final check.
tr.check.ledger_not_compared: A ledger ({cases} cases) exists but this result has no e2e results, so it was not compared.
style.none: No style set. Follow the style and words already in the file.
style.no_template: Brief template `{name}` not found (impl, fix, mockup, research, review, docs, test).
style.haeyo.name: Friendly UI voice
style.haeyo.line: Friendly UI voice: short, one topic per screen. No question titles, dash-joined sentences, abbreviations or decorative explanation. (`wb-style rules haeyo`)
style.report.name: Report voice
style.report.line: Report voice: state and problem first, one fact per sentence. No narration of the work, hype or unsupported judgements. (`wb-style rules report`)
style.plain.name: Plain voice
style.plain.line: Short sentences. Follow the wording already in the file; no emoji or decoration. (`wb-style rules plain`)
rules.check.ok: The rule catalog has no problems ({count} rules).
rules.md.title: Rule catalog
rules.md.intro: Each rule lists why it exists, where it is enforced and how to recover when it blocks you. This file is generated by `wb-rules render --write`; do not edit it by hand.
xp.clear: Nothing is blocked or waiting right now.
xp.links.none: No linked documents. Link some under `explain.links` in the project settings.
xp.config_broken.what: The settings have {count} error(s). The first is {key} in {file}.
xp.config_broken.why: With broken settings the safety rules cannot tell what to block, so anything risky is blocked.
xp.config_broken.fix: Run `/wb:doctor`, fix the error, then confirm with `wb-config validate`.
xp.limit.what: The {model} model hit its usage limit. It frees up at {until}.
xp.limit.why: An agent cannot start on a model that is out of quota, and wb will not go below the lowest model set for a task type.
xp.limit.fix: Run `wb-route explain <task>` to see the next usable model. If all are out, wait until {until}; with auto-retry on, work resumes then.
xp.limit_all.what: The account hit its usage limit. It frees up at {until}.
xp.limit_all.why: No model can start a new agent.
xp.limit_all.fix: Wait until {until}. With auto-retry on, work resumes then (`/wb:auto-retry status`).
xp.gate_lock.what: A verification gate is running, so merging is paused.
xp.gate_lock.why: If code changes while the gate runs, its result no longer belongs to a known commit.
xp.gate_lock.fix: Wait for the gate to finish. If it looks stuck, check `wb-reap`; clearing needs the owner to run `wb-reap --gate-lock`.
xp.lane_dead.what: Lane {lane} is marked running but has been idle for {min} min.
xp.lane_dead.why: The agent has probably stopped or hit a limit.
xp.lane_dead.fix: Run `/wb:resume` to plan the restart and start the lane again in its own worktree.
xp.lane_blocked.why: The lane marked itself unable to proceed, usually waiting for a decision or another lane.
xp.lane_blocked.fix: Read the lane's note (`wb-waves board`) and make the decision it needs.
xp.lane_failed.why: The agent ended with an error or review sent it back.
xp.lane_failed.fix: Check the last state with `/wb:resume`, put the reason in the brief and start it again.
xp.lane_review.why: The agent has finished and its result needs checking.
xp.progress_stale.what: {file} is older than the latest work.
xp.progress_stale.why: A new session continues from this file alone, so a stale one repeats finished work.
xp.progress_stale.fix: Write what is done, in progress and next, then commit.
xp.progress_missing.why: A session that picks up the work has nothing to read.
xp.progress_missing.fix: Create it with `/wb:init` or write the current state.
xp.lane_dirty.what: Lane {lane} has {count} uncommitted change(s) in its worktree.
xp.lane_dirty.why: Uncommitted changes can be lost when a session ends.
xp.lane_dirty.fix: If the lane will use them, save them in a temporary commit. Discard only after the owner agrees.
xp.worktree_missing.what: The worktree {path} of lane {lane} is gone.
xp.worktree_missing.why: The ledger lists the lane but its folder is missing, so work cannot continue.
xp.worktree_missing.fix: Recreate it with `wb-worktree create {lane}`, or for a finished lane tidy the ledger with `wb-reap --apply`.
xp.worktree_unregistered.what: Worktree {path} (branch {branch}) is not in the lane ledger.
xp.worktree_unregistered.why: Nobody is known to own it, which makes cleanup hard.
xp.worktree_unregistered.fix: Leave it if in use; if finished, merge it and remove it with `wb-worktree remove`.
xp.lanes_full.what: {count} live lanes: the cap of {max} is reached.
xp.lanes_full.why: Too many lanes raise machine load and tests time out.
xp.lanes_full.fix: Land finished lanes and clean up their worktrees before opening another (`/wb:lanes`).
xp.slots_busy.what: All {kind} run slots are in use ({count} held).
xp.slots_busy.why: Running heavy jobs together slows the machine and causes false failures, so only the slot count may run.
xp.slots_busy.fix: See who holds them with `wb-slot status` and wait. `wb-reap` reclaims slots whose owner died.
xp.on_protected.what: You are on the protected branch `{branch}`.
xp.on_protected.why: Commits and merges there need the owner's grant.
xp.on_protected.fix: Work on a feature or lane branch. The owner grants landing with `/wb:approve`.
work.step.understand: Restate the request in one sentence and confirm it with the user
work.step.find: A research lane looks and reports; no files change
work.step.answer: Tell the user what was found in plain words
work.step.reproduce: A research lane reproduces the problem and reports likely causes
work.step.fix: A fix lane repairs the cause and adds a regression test
work.step.brief: Write the brief and check it with `wb-check brief`
work.step.build: An implementation lane builds it as the brief says
work.step.review: A different model reviews it in a fresh context
work.step.integrate: Merge the reviewed lane into the integration branch
work.step.report: Report: what was checked and what remains, kept apart
work.step.mockup: A mockup lane draws the current and proposed screens
work.step.decide: The owner chooses from the mockups (`/wb:decide`)
work.step.write: A docs lane writes by the style rules (`wb-style`)
work.step.harness: Design track check: a large design can run in the separate design plugin
work.step.design: A design lane drafts the proposal
work.step.record: Update `progress.md` and tell the user to `/clear`
work.harness.installed: The design plugin (king-wjang-harness) is installed; you can use its track.
work.harness.missing: The design plugin (king-wjang-harness) is not installed. Ask the user whether to install it; wb does not depend on it.
decide.bad_slug: `{slug}` is not a valid decision name (letters, digits, `-`, `_`).
decide.need_options: At least two options are needed: --option "A=text".
decide.bad_recommend: Recommendation `{key}` is not one of the options.
decide.commit_hint: Commit suggestion: `git add {file}` and commit. Nothing is committed automatically.
decide.ambiguous: More than one decision file matches `{key}`; give the full file name.
safety.codegraph.no_index.why: `{path}` has no codegraph index. A call for this path already failed in this session, so another one fails the same way.
safety.codegraph.no_index.fix: It is in the index queue (`wb-index status`). Until the index exists, continue with grep and Read.
safety.codegraph.no_index_manual.why: `{path}` has no codegraph index. A call for this path already failed in this session, so another one fails the same way.
safety.codegraph.no_index_manual.fix: Continue with grep and Read. To build the index, queue it with `wb-index add {path}`.
cg.nudge: Callers of `{ident}` come back with their enclosing functions in one `codegraph_callers` call (projectPath: `{root}`). Use codegraph for flow and callers, grep for line numbers and strings. This note shows once per session.
cg.dead_notice: `{path}` has no codegraph index{queued}. Do not call codegraph for this path again; continue with grep and Read.
cg.missing: codegraph is not installed. `/wb:init` installs it only after you agree (for example `brew install codegraph`).
cg.not_git: `{path}` is not a git checkout, so it was not queued.
cg.worker_busy: Another index worker (pid {pid}) is working through the queue.
cg.usage: usage: wb-index add [path] | run | status | drop <path> | orphans [--apply] | metrics [--days N] [--json]
cg.orphans_none: No leftover indexes (indexes in folders that are no longer worktrees).
cg.orphans_fix: `wb-index orphans --apply` deletes only these indexes (the folders stay).
wt.index_queued: Added to the codegraph index queue (`wb-index status`).
doctor.codegraphOrphans.detail: {count} · {size} — list them with `wb-index orphans`, clean up with `--apply`
